title: fix(spec): composeStacks says why a top-level connector beside a package body's same-named entry is ambiguous

This PR touches the published spec (`packages/spec/src/**`), so it lands only after a full review at the reviewer tier and a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` contract review record PASS on the current head.

Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** #27939 的合成检查里，有一种情形的拒收理由不对：包体里的连接器和产物顶层的同名连接器一个能出借、一个不能。原提示说「运行时每个包各留一条，先注册的出借」。实际上，开机时顶层那条不注册，由包体那条出借；开发态重载时，顶层那条会替换包体那条。现在提示写明这一点；`slot` 文档和 `providedCollectionEntries` 的说明也写清了。另外改了一个测试名，并补了 `preserve` 下混合嵌套输入的测试。
- **为什么改：** 结论正确但理由错误，会误导作者判断该改哪一条声明。
- **风险与回滚：** 接受集不变：原来拒收的仍拒收，原来通过的仍通过，只改提示文字。两个包体之间冲突的提示一字未改。回滚即 revert。
- **先看：** `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 中 `collectComposedDatasourceConnectorErrors` 的歧义分支，以及 `ProvidedCollectionEntry.inBody` 的文档。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/stack-datasource-connector.test.ts`，预期 30 个测试全过。
- **需要您做的：** 无（需审阅档全量复审与合约复审 PASS）。

## What changes

- **`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`:**
  - `ProvidedCollectionEntry` gains `inBody`: whether the entry boots as a package body's own item. That covers an entry of a `packages[]` body, and, under `preserve`, the top level of an input that `preservePackageEntries` folds into a body of its own id. Its doc states the mechanism for every other top-level entry beside package bodies. The residual rule (`unclaimedTopLevel`) does not register such an entry when a body declares its name. When no body declares the name, the rule registers it under the composed artifact's `manifest.id` (the last input's). A dev reload replaces the booted entries of the name with the artifact's top-level list (`mergeDeclaredConnectorSources`). So its `slot` (`'artifact'`, or a mixed `preserve` input's own `package:${id}`) is a stand-in. It stays a stand-in because keeping it apart from the bodies is what refuses the boot-or-reload split as ambiguous.
  - The ambiguity finding now names the mechanism that applies:
    - **Two package bodies:** unchanged, byte for byte ("the runtime keeps one entry per package and lends from whichever registers first").
    - **A package body and a top-level entry:** "which the composed artifact declares both in a package body and at its top level, … The boot does not register a top-level entry whose name a package body declares, so the body's entry lends, and a dev reload replaces it with the artifact's top-level entries of the name, the first of which lends, so the entry the datasource borrows depends on whether the artifact was booted or reloaded and on the order of its inputs."
    - **Top-level entries of two inputs, beside bodies that do not declare the name:** a sentence of its own: no door registers either as a package body's entry, and a dev reload lends from the first top-level entry of the name.
  - `providedCollectionEntries`' docblock and `collectComposedDatasourceConnectorErrors`' docblock say the same.
- **`packages/spec/src/stack-datasource-connector.test.ts`:**
  - "treats a package body and another input's top level as two slots" is renamed to "refuses as ambiguous a top-level entry beside a package body's same-named entry, and names the body". It now asserts the new sentence and the absence of "one entry per package".
  - A new group pins the `preserve` reading of an input that carries `packages` beside its own top-level `connectors`. With a descriptor at its top level and another package's lending instance, it is refused as ambiguous, with the beside-a-body sentence, in both input orders. With two lending instances it composes in both orders. The composed artifact keeps that top level beside the inner and plain bodies only, under the last input's `manifest.id`, and the whole flattened `connectors` list in input order (pinned both ways, since a dev reload lends from the first). Two such inputs whose top-level entries disagree, beside bodies silent on the name, are refused with the top-level-only sentence in both orders.
- **`.changeset/28006-composed-connector-ambiguity-reason.md`:** `@objectstack/spec` `patch` (the message text ships), both declaration lines, and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker.

## Why

Should-fix 1 of contract record 6516406275 on PR #27939: the refusal was right for a reason the message, the slot doc and the test name did not give.

## Verification

All on head `541d7f5b3d` (should-fixes 1 and 2 of contract record 6519281283 in 15802379bc, then a merge of `origin/main`).

- **Verdicts unchanged:** the 30 tests were run against `origin/main`'s `stack.zod.ts`. The 25 that do not assert the new wording passed. The 5 that do failed only on that wording: each first asserted the envelope (`STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`, 422) and exactly one finding for the datasource, and those assertions passed. So every composition this file covers is refused or accepted exactly as before.
- **Ablation:** with the mixed input's top level judged in the composed artifact's slot instead of its own, both orders of the mixed `preserve` refusal go red, and the mixed-first order is accepted. The 26 other cases stay green. Restored, 28/28 pass (measured on `55b0c85641`, before the two cases should-fix 2 added).
- **Package:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, `test` and `typecheck` under the verify lock: build exit 0; 756 test files passed, 22505 tests passed (1 todo); typecheck passed (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- **Local gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, derived after merging `origin/main`, named 80 families (re-derived after the second merge of `origin/main`). All were run, with exit codes recorded before any pipe, and every one exited 0. `dispatch-gates --ran`: "80 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 80 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)". The tree was clean after the gate run, so no generated reference moved. The full gate battery is CI's. Dogfood was not run: `Clause-②: no` does not owe it, and no verdict moves.

## Acceptance notes

- **The slot stays a stand-in on purpose.** Judging a mixed input's top level in the composed artifact's `manifest.id` slot, where the residual rule registers it, would move a verdict: with the plain input last, a descriptor at the mixed input's top level would be judged last-wins against the plain body's instance and accepted. The card forbids that, so the doc states the mechanism instead.
- **Worktree:** `objectstack-issue-28006` on the claimed branch, as the Claim names.
